note: A sample handbook, invented, so the playground works before anyone uploads anything. Written so that the useful answers share no words with the questions a new person actually asks.
title: Sample: a small team handbook
text:
Annual leave is requested through the staff portal. Give two weeks notice where you can, and your lead approves it in the same place.

Expenses under two hundred are reimbursed without approval. Anything above that needs a line manager to sign it off before you spend it, not after.

The deployment pipeline runs on every push to main. A red build blocks the merge, and the person who broke it fixes it before starting anything else.

New starters are paired with a buddy for their first month. The buddy answers the questions that are too small to raise in a standup.

We are asynchronous by default. Nobody is expected to answer outside their own working hours, and no meeting is booked without an agenda in the invitation.

Customer data never leaves our own machines. Anything that would send it to a third party goes through a review before it is written, not before it ships.

Hardware is replaced every three years, or sooner if it is holding you up. Ask; the answer is usually yes.

The on-call rota is one week long and rotates on Monday morning. Whoever is on call is not expected to do project work that week.
